subject: Service availability slab & latency window harmonization
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@nimbusware.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Anders <tom.anders@nimbusware.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft SLA: uptime % and monthly remedy proposal

Evelyn — thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is our redline of your standard SLA (see Nimbus_SLA_Redline_v2.pdf). High level asks from procurement/engineering: 

- Baseline uptime: 99.95% (we need a firm anchor for contract reporting)
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms for hosted API (we're sensitive to tail latency)
- Monthly remedy: automated credit up to 30% of monthly invoice for sustained breaches (this is our starting position; we can discuss caps)
- Maintenance: we need clarity on planned maintenance windows and whether those count toward uptime (our preference is a measurement window carveout for scheduled regional maintenance)

Can you confirm Redwood's position on the above and flag any non-starters? We're aiming to finalize SLA terms ahead of board review next week.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick sync if helpful.

--
Sarah Lee
Sr. Procurement Manager | NimbusWare, Inc.
procurement@nimbusware.com
+1 (415) 555-0143
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@nimbusware.com>
Cc: Tom Anders <tom.anders@nimbusware.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft SLA: uptime % and monthly remedy proposal

Sarah — thanks for the redline and for laying out Nimbus's priorities. We've reviewed with product and ops; below are Redwood's counterpoints and a suggested compromise to keep the commercial process moving: 

1) Baseline uptime
- We can commit to a 99.95% monthly availability for the Hosted API for production routes you pin to the contract.
- We request a limited maintenance carveout policy: up to 4 hours/month of scheduled maintenance per region (not charged against uptime) provided 72-hour notice and scheduling within agreed maintenance windows. Unexpected incidents still count against uptime.

2) Latency (p95)
- We can target p95 <= 250ms for typical single-request synthetic traffic on standard models in our hosted catalog.
- Important caveat: latency SLOs depend on model family and request size. We'll include an appendix mapping pinned routes to model profiles; if Nimbus pins larger models or long-sequence workloads, p95 will need to be adjusted.

3) Monthly remedy / credit structure
- We propose a tiered remedy ladder instead of a single 30% cap:
  * 99.9% - 99.95% => 5% credit of monthly invoice
  * 99.5% - 99.9% => 15% credit
  * <99.5% => 30% credit
- We recommend a hard cap of 30% per month and a cumulative annual cap equal to 2x monthly invoice to limit open financial exposure while still offering meaningful remedies.

4) Measurement windows & monitoring
- Credits will be calculated from our monitoring (token-level success/latency logs). We'll share read-only dashboards and daily digests for the pilot month.

Next steps: attaching our computed credit schedule (computed_credits_breakdown.xlsx) and a marked-up template showing the maintenance carveout language. If you can confirm which routes/models Nimbus intends to pin, we can finalize the latency appendix.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call to close this out tomorrow.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
+1 (650) 555-0210

Subject: Internal: Nimbus SLA counter — commercial and risk notes

Eve — quick internal note after reading your reply to Nimbus: 

- The tiered remedy ladder looks good commercially. Procurement will push for a flat 30% cap but should be manageable.
- Ask legal whether 'annual cumulative cap = 2x monthly invoice' needs to be restated as 'aggregate cap' — probably fine but needs explicit language.
- Pricing team wants to confirm whether the credit tiers apply to invoice net of credits or gross invoice (i.e., credits shouldn't cascade). I can loop in pricing if you'd like.

Operational/technical: cc'ing Marissa — can you confirm the 4 hours/month scheduled maintenance carveout per region is operationally feasible? Also, if Nimbus wants model pinning for lower-latency families, what's the delta on price?

I'll be on a call at 3pm; if you want me to join the sync with Sarah/Tom I can make time.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Sales & Renewals | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 15:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Nimbus SLA counter — ops feasibility

Ben / Eve — operational clarifications from infra: 

- 4 hours/month per region is acceptable as scheduled maintenance carveout, provided Nimbus agrees to the maintenance window constraints (2am-5am PT preferred for US). We'll add an escalation channel for urgent maintenance with a postmortem within 48 hours.
- Latency p95 <= 250ms is achievable on the 'latency-optimized' model family for small requests (<=512 tokens). For larger payloads we recommend moving to a dedicated capacity plan or accepting a higher p95 in the latency appendix.
- Price delta for pinned latency-optimized model family: ~20% uplift on per-token billing or the option to move to a dedicated node pool (we can show cost comparisons in the next doc).

I updated the computed_credits_breakdown.xlsx with example remediation math for a typical Nimbus monthly spend and included a sheet that demonstrates how credits do not cascade.

Marissa
Sr. Product Ops Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@nimbusware.com>, Tom Anders <tom.anders@nimbusware.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft SLA: uptime % and monthly remedy proposal — Redwood response

Sarah / Tom — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the flexibility on measurement language. To summarize and propose final edits we can sign: 

- Availability: Redwood will commit to 99.95% monthly availability for pinned production routes.
- Maintenance carveout: scheduled maintenance up to 4 hours/month per region (2am-5am PT preferred) with 72 hours' notice and 48-hour post-maintenance report.
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms for pinned routes using latency-optimized family on requests <=512 tokens. For other cases we'll include a latency appendix with explicit model mappings.
- Remedy: tiered credit ladder (5% / 15% / 30%) with a monthly cap of 30% and annual aggregate cap of 2x monthly invoice. Credits calculated from Redwood monitoring; we will publish read-only dashboards for the pilot month.

Attached are: (1) the redline we discussed (Nimbus_SLA_Redline_v2.pdf) with our edits, and (2) computed_credits_breakdown.xlsx showing sample math. If Nimbus confirms the pinned routes/models list and accepts the maintenance window language, we'll move the SLA into signature-ready form.

Can you confirm by end-of-day Friday? If you'd prefer a short call, Ben and I are available Thursday 10:00–11:00 PT.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
